item.title: Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Ionic Digital (IOND) Sells 737 Bitcoin to Fund Data Center Buildout Ionic Digital (IOND) sold about 737 bitcoin after the end of September for roughly $61.6 million and plans to spend the money building out its data center sites, the miner built from Celsius’ old mining business disclosed in its latest quarterly report. The company said in its 10-Q that the coins sold at an average of $83,600 each, net of trading costs. The sales cut its bitcoin holdings by about 25% from the Sept. 30 balance. Ionic held 2,954 bitcoin at the end of the third quarter, up from 2,719 at the end of 2025. That implies about 2,217 bitcoin left after the sales. “The Company intends to use the proceeds to fund the development of its existing data center sites,” the filing said. The filing does not say when the coins were sold. Bitcoin traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, about 23% below Ionic’s average sale price. From Celsius miner to landlord Ionic was formed in January 2024 to take over the assets of Celsius Mining under the bankrupt lender’s Chapter 11 plan. It started out as a pure bitcoin miner, running fleets of ASIC machines at its own and hosted sites. That changed in October 2025, when it signed a lease with a single tenant for its Ward County, Texas, facility, which it previously called Cedarvale. The lease runs through January 2037. The third quarter shows how far the shift has gone, with revenue rising to about $49.0 million from $37.1 million a year earlier. Digital infrastructure leasing brought in $43.9 million of that, while mining revenue fell to $5.1 million from $37.1 million. Ionic swung to a net profit of $17.4 million for the quarter, compared with a $4.5 million loss a year earlier. That result included a $73.2 million gain on the fair value of its bitcoin, offset in part by a $65.9 million loss from remeasuring warrants. For the first nine months of the year, Ionic posted a net loss of $30.9 million. More capacity for the tenant In February, Ionic amended the Ward County lease. The tenant is now obligated to lease another 89 megawatts of capacity when it becomes available. Control of that added capacity had not passed to the tenant by the end of September, so Ionic has not booked any revenue on it. The company also had about $19.6 million left to pay on transformer purchases and a substation expansion at the site. The conversion has cost Ionic mining capacity. The company said it does not have room at its owned and leased sites to relocate all of the miners it used to run, so it has decommissioned some of them. Ionic went public through a direct listing on July 28 and raised $400 million in a private placement before $16.7 million in costs. It had about $381.4 million in cash and equivalents at Sept. 30. A familiar trade Ionic is one of several public miners turning bitcoin into cash for AI and data center projects this month. MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin for $1.1 billion and said more sales were coming. item.title: German Court Offers to Drop Movie2k Case for 40,000 Bitcoin
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine German Court Offers to Drop Movie2k Case for 40,000 Bitcoin A Leipzig judge last week offered to dismiss the criminal case against the alleged operator of the defunct Movie2k piracy site if he hands over 40,000 bitcoin, a stake worth about $2.56 billion at current prices. The presiding judge at the Leipzig Regional Court, Karsten Nickel, made the proposal in a trial that began in February. A spokesman for the Dresden prosecutors’ office confirmed it after German newspapers and the public broadcaster MDR first reported the offer. Heise later published a detailed account. The trial is before the court’s economic criminal chamber, and the Leipzig court itself had not issued its own confirmation when prosecutors spoke to reporters. Prosecutors believe the defendant still holds about 56,000 bitcoin, and transferring 40,000 would leave him roughly 16,000 coins. At a bitcoin price of about $64,000, those 16,000 coins would be worth about $1.02 billion, and forty thousand bitcoin would be worth about $2.56 billion at the same price. The dollar figures are approximate. Cash, a waiver and leftover coins The proposal also calls for him to pay €38 million in compensation for potential victims, including film rights holders, MDR reported . He would also have to give up any claim to the roughly €2.64 billion Saxony already raised from bitcoin he transferred in 2024, the newspaper Freie Presse reported . Even after handing over most of the remaining coins, he could leave court a billionaire. Movie2k.to ran from 2008 until it was shut down in May 2013. Prosecutors say its operators made millions from advertising contracts and used the proceeds to buy bitcoin when the price was far lower. The defendant is charged with commercial money laundering in 146 cases. The court has already ruled that about 220,000 copyright counts are time-barred and are no longer part of the Movie2k case. A co-defendant, a Polish national, is charged with money laundering in 46 cases and especially serious tax evasion. Prosecutors say he received bitcoin from the main defendant in May 2013 as pay for work on the site. Nickel has said that proof of some of the charges would face “great difficulties.” It is conceivable, he said, that legally and illegally obtained bitcoin were mixed in the accounts. German authorities already sold nearly 50,000 bitcoin German authorities had sought the defendant internationally since late 2019. He was arrested abroad in May 2023 and held in pretrial detention in Saxony until mid-January 2024. On Jan. 16, 2024, he voluntarily transferred about 49,858 bitcoin to wallets provided by the Federal Criminal Police Office. At the time, the coins were worth about €1.96 billion, and he was released from detention around the time of that transfer. Saxony sold the coins between June 19 and July 12, 2024, with support from the Federal Criminal Police Office, for €2,639,683,413.92, or about €2.64 billion. item.title: Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam Coinbase (COIN) said its AI scam-prevention agent stopped about $4.7 million in customer funds from reaching scammers who used a deepfake of Elon Musk to pitch a fake Tesla crypto giveaway, blocking roughly 91% of the money customers tried to send. The exchange described the incident in a Tuesday blog post, part of a weekly series on consumer protection. It said the system worked “with no humans in the loop.” Those two figures imply customers tried to send about $5.2 million, and that roughly $460,000 still left their accounts. Coinbase did not say how much reached the scammers. A livestream that wasn’t real The scam ran during Tesla’s “flying car” demo. Scammers set up a YouTube livestream that looked like the real broadcast, with a deepfake Musk, on-screen wallet addresses and a QR code. The stream promised to double any crypto sent to it, and more than half a million people watched, Coinbase said. Over about two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers tried to send millions of dollars to the addresses on screen. Many were long-time users. Coinbase did not say when the fake stream ran or which coins customers tried to send. The company stressed that its platform was not breached. “Nobody was hacked,” Coinbase wrote. “No Coinbase account was broken into, no password stolen, no credential phished.” That is what makes giveaway fraud hard to stop, since most defenses look for activity the account holder did not authorize, and here the customers logged in and pressed confirm themselves. “Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent,” the post said. How the agent works Coinbase said its defense has three parts. Machine learning models first score outgoing sends in real time, watching for giveaway patterns, brand impersonation and newly created wallet addresses. The goal, the company wrote, is “to catch the danger, not the customer.” When a send is flagged, a scam-specific agent takes over, looking up context, naming the scam pattern, explaining how giveaway schemes work and asking questions meant to make the story fall apart. Each reply is scored for confidence before the customer sees it, so the system knows when a situation needs more friction. The agent had never been trained on this kind of con, Coinbase said. Deepfake giveaways tied to a live product launch were not in its training data. “It recognized the shape of the scheme anyway,” the company wrote, pointing to the promise to multiply funds, the deadline of a live event and a transfer that could not be reversed. Cheaper fakes Coinbase said deepfakes have changed the economics of the scam. Staging something like this once took “a crew, a studio, and weeks,” it wrote. “Now it takes a livestream slot and a model.” The company said it is expanding AI review of risky sends to every type of scam, not just high-profile ones, and is also using AI to label new scam cases so its models learn fro

item.title: New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York State Pension Fund Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake by More Than 10% The New York State Common Retirement Fund raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by more than 10% in the third quarter, to 352,850 shares worth $54.0 million at Sept. 30. The pension fund disclosed the position in a Form 13F filed Tuesday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. It added 33,000 shares from the 319,850 it reported at June 30. That is an increase of a little more than 10%. The filing does not say why the pension fund added the shares. The reported value nearly doubled, to $54.0 million from $27.8 million. Strategy’s stock closed the quarter at $153.09, up from $86.93 at midyear, so most of the gain in dollar value came from the rally, not from the added shares. A small slice of a large pension fund The fund is one of the largest public pension plans in the U.S. It holds the assets used to pay retirement benefits for New York’s state and local public employees. Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli, the fund’s trustee, valued it at an estimated $309.7 billion as of June 30, the latest official figure. There is not yet a published valuation for Sept. 30. Public equities are only part of the portfolio. As of March 31, they accounted for 39.4% of the fund’s assets, with the rest in cash and bonds, private equity, real estate and other alternatives. The 13F lists 2,975 holdings worth $71.3 billion. The Strategy stake is a small slice of that book, less than a tenth of a percent. Strategy has made bitcoin its primary treasury asset. The company held 850,849 bitcoin as of Nov. 15, with an aggregate purchase price of $64.20 billion, or $75,452 a coin. Institutional managers have 45 days after quarter-end to file a 13F. Tuesday’s report is the first official look at the pension fund’s third-quarter buying, after the stock had already fallen sharply from the $153.09 price used in the filing. Strategy shares have already fallen Strategy closed Tuesday at $96.50, below $100 and about 37% under its Sept. 30 close. At that price, the same 352,850 shares are worth about $34 million, roughly $20 million less than the value in the filing. The common shares also finished under Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, which closed at $98.70. That is the first time they have closed below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close of $121.07. A 13F is a snapshot. It does not show whether the pension fund bought or sold shares in October or November, when most of that decline took place. Coinbase and miners, but no bitcoin ETFs The information table lists no shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust or other spot bitcoin ETFs, and no shares of Strategy’s preferred stock. The pension fund does hold Coinbase (COIN). It reported 109,433 shares at Sept. 30, a little below the 111,633 shares it held at midyear. The reported value still rose, to $20.4 million from $16.3 million, as Coinbase’s stock climbed. It also holds a string of bitcoin miners.

item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 as Fed’s Waller Floats Half-Point Hike Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Wednesday morning, according to Bitcoin Magazine data, as Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point rate hike is probably needed in December. The bitcoin price had slipped below $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon. It climbed back to about $65,000 that evening after Nvidia beat earnings estimates, then faded through the U.S. morning. The bitcoin price is down about 21% from a month ago, when it traded above $81,000. Waller floats a half-point hike Waller told CNBC in a live interview that the Fed probably needs a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He said the central bank should reverse its three quarter-point cuts from last year and may need to do more. “You might need to, like, shock people,” Waller said. “I’m very, very concerned about inflation. It’s kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” he said. Waller said the Fed should deliver the larger move if it is not prepared to signal a faster pace of hikes in the coming months. He also said about 70% of items in the core services basket are running above 3%, which has nothing to do with oil. The 2-year Treasury yield rose more than 4 basis points to 4.83% after his comments. The dollar hit a 19-month high, and gold dropped 2.5% to its lowest level in more than a year. Futures markets fully price a quarter-point hike in December and another increase in January, CNBC reported. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem suggested Tuesday that as many as four hikes could come by spring. Minutes from the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting are due Wednesday afternoon. Policymakers held rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, with Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike. Nvidia lifts tech stocks Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.84 billion after the bell Tuesday, more than double a year earlier and above the $109.1 billion analysts expected. Data center revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, and the company guided to about $130 billion for the current quarter. Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will remain “disciplined in how we commit capital.” The board said it would not reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO last week. Nvidia shares were up about 2.6% in premarket trading. Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.8% and S&P 500 futures rose 0.3%, but the bitcoin price did not follow tech higher. IREN (IREN), the bitcoin miner turned AI cloud provider, rose between 8% and 10% in extended trading along with CoreWeave and Nebius, and was recently up about 3% premarket. Strategy (MSTR) closed down 6.3% at $96.50 on Tuesday and was little changed before the open, while Coinbase (COIN) closed down 4% and was up about 0.5% premarket. item.title: South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says South Korea’s Financial Services Commission plans to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report . The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release. The FSC itself has not publicly announced a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025. A roadmap that stalled That plan opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit. Exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived. The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate. What the Basic Act adds The Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week. Lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Min Byung-duk of the Democratic Party said at a recent forum that he intends to “wrap it up by Jan. 9.” The 5% question The report did not describe what the corporate guidelines will contain. In January, *Seoul Economic Daily* reported that a draft would cap a company’s annual crypto investment at 5% of equity capital and limit purchases to the top 20 coins by market value. item.title: Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips Below $64,000 as Strategy (MSTR) Falls Below $100 Bitcoin price slipped near $64,000 on Tuesday afternoon, as Strategy (MSTR) and Coinbase (COIN) shares fell and traders waited on Nvidia’s first earnings report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. The bitcoin price had climbed back to about $65,000 before the U.S. open, after holding near that level on Monday. Selling picked up once stocks turned lower, and bitcoin price slipped to about $63,300 at its low. Strategy and Coinbase shares slide Strategy shares were recently down more than 5% to about $97, dropping below $100 and trading under the company’s STRC preferred stock, which was little changed near $99. It is the first time the common has traded below the preferred since mid-August. The stock is also down about 20% from its Nov. 10 close near $121. Strategy added 485 bitcoin last week, lifting its holdings to 850,849 BTC. The shares have kept falling with the bitcoin price. Coinbase was recently down about 3% to about $116. Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) dropped about 4% and 5%. Bitcoin miners were mostly lower. MARA Holdings (MARA), CleanSpark (CLSK) and IREN (IREN) each fell about 3% to 4%, and Cipher Mining (CIFR) was down about 2%. Hut 8 (HUT) was a modest exception, recently up about 1%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) were little changed, while Core Scientific (CORZ) and BitMine (BMNR) were also lower. Nvidia earnings weigh on stocks The broader market was also weaker late in the session. The chipmaker reports results after the bell, with analysts expecting revenue of about $109 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress will lead her first earnings call in the role. Huang, in his first public statement since resigning last week, said he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and America.
